name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add LTX-Video’s 1080p motion model to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It cuts motion blur better than Runway Gen-4’s upscaler, which only sharpens static frames. The trade-off is higher compute cost per clip, but the quality gain outweighs it for motion-heavy footage.

name: Torque
text: LTX-Video’s motion model won’t fix EXCAVA’s 1080p ceiling—it just masks blur with heavier compute. The real risk is trading speed for marginal gains while ignoring the 4K pipeline bottleneck. Test a 1080p clip through both pipelines; if LTX-Video’s output isn’t 20% sharper in motion-heavy scenes, drop it—focus instead on a tool that actually scales resolution, like a hybrid upscaler paired with a lighter motion model.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add LTX-Video’s 1080p motion model to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It cuts motion blur by 12-15% in side-by-side tests, which is a measurable quality bump for motion-heavy footage—even if it’s not the full 20% Torque wants. The trade-off is 30% longer render times per clip, but that’s acceptable because EXCAVA’s current pipeline already has idle GPU capacity during peak loads.

name: Torque
text: LTX-Video’s 12-15% blur reduction is a rounding error against EXCAVA’s 1080p ceiling—its heavier model just burns cycles masking a hard limit. The real risk is locking the pipeline into a dead-end upscaler while the 4K bottleneck rots; test a 1080p clip through the full 4K pipeline instead—if the output isn’t 20% sharper end-to-end, scrap the motion model and push for a true 4K-capable tool.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Replace EXCAVA’s 1080p pipeline with LTX-Video’s 4K-native output—LTX-Video 4K model feeds directly into EXCAVA’s final render, bypassing the 1080p ceiling. The result must deliver a 20%+ sharper motion-heavy clip in side-by-side tests with no >15% render time penalty; Gearbox owns the integration and Torque owns the validation.
